title: Hand out alerts while subscribers come and go

blocks.text: The on-call system hands each alert to its subscribers: the pager, the chat bridge, the SMS gateway, the escalation timer. Subscribers change the list while they handle an alert. When the pager reaches someone, it unsubscribes the SMS gateway, so the person isn't texted as well. The escalation timer unsubscribes itself once an alert is acknowledged. A new audit subscriber may be added halfway through.

The engineer on call wrote this on Monday's incident: "Paged, answered, and still got the SMS a second later." Finish `publish(String alert)` in `src/main/java/practice/AlertBus.java`, which keeps its subscribers in a `CopyOnWriteArrayList`:

items: a subscriber unsubscribed before its turn comes doesn't get the alert;
one subscribed during an alert starts with the next alert;
everyone else gets it once, in the order they subscribed.

cases.says: with no changes during an alert, every subscriber gets each alert once, in the order they subscribed
a subscriber unsubscribed by another during an alert, before its turn, does not get that alert
a subscriber added while an alert is handed out does not get that alert
a subscriber that unsubscribes itself during an alert does not keep the subscriber after it from getting the alert

origin.section: A CopyOnWriteArrayList Iterator Walks the Array It Started With

concepts: A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator walks the array current when it was created: an element removed during the walk is still visited and one added is not.
